en.headline: Insurance Authority moves to tighten oversight of premium financing market
en.dek: The regulator says aggressive marketing and high leverage have drawn middle-class buyers into arrangements once limited to high-net-worth clients, and a joint inspection with the HKMA continues.
body: Hong Kong’s Insurance Authority is strengthening oversight of the premium financing market after the practice grew rapidly and spread beyond its traditional high-net-worth clientele.

Premium financing allows policyholders to borrow from banks or other lenders to pay large upfront premiums on life insurance policies. In the first half of 2026, such arrangements accounted for about 36 per cent of new business premiums, up from 19 per cent in 2025, according to the authority.

Marty Lui, the Insurance Authority’s executive director of long-term business, told a media briefing that some insurers had promoted the product too aggressively by lowering thresholds and using high leverage. Products with leverage of nine times or more have appeared, meaning buyers put up less than 10 per cent of the premium.

The authority and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority have been conducting a joint inspection since June and expect to complete it by the end of the year. Officials said they would then consider appropriate regulatory measures, particularly on affordability assessments, while avoiding rules that could force abrupt market disruption.

zh.headline: 保監局加強保費融資市場監管 指高槓桿及進取推廣存風險
zh.dek: 監管局表示，進取市場推廣及高槓桿吸引中產買家，與金管局聯合查察預計年底完成。
body: 香港保險業監管局正加強保費融資市場的監管，因該安排迅速擴張，並已超出傳統高資產淨值客戶範圍。
保費融資讓保單持有人向銀行或其他貸款機構借款，支付大額壽險保單的首期保費。監管局數據顯示，2026年上半年，相關安排佔新造業務保費約36%，較2025年的19%上升。
保監局長遠業務執行董事呂愈國在傳媒簡報會上表示，部分保險公司透過降低門檻及高槓桿進取推廣。市場出現九倍或以上槓桿產品，買家只需支付少於一成保費。
保監局與金管局自6月起進行聯合查察，預計年底前完成。官員表示其後會考慮適當監管措施，尤其是負擔能力評估，同時避免突然擾亂市場的規則。
